The estimated average treatment effect on the controls (ATC) is about 4.01.

The data only show each child's outcome under the group they were actually in, so I had to estimate the missing outcomes. I fitted a linear regression of `y` on all 25 covariates using the treated children only. I used it to predict what each control child's score would have been with treatment. The ATC is the mean of those predictions minus the controls' observed scores.

The mirror-image approach gives a similar number. Fitting on controls only and predicting for treated children, then comparing with the treated group's observed mean, gives 3.94. I went with the first because it estimates the effect on the controls directly.

ANSWER: 4.01
